simple.meaning: מַצָּב (matstsâb) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a fixed spot ; figuratively, an office , a military post.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Joshua 4:3. The surrounding context includes family, family line, covenant, priesthood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַצָּב (H4673) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מַצָּב (matstsâb) / H4673 is traced through Joshua 4:3, Joshua 4:9, 1 Samuel 13:23, 1 Samuel 14:1 with generated occurrence evidence.

majorEvents.evidenceText: The garrison of the Philistines went out to the pass of Michmash.

timeline.evidenceText: and command them, saying, ‘Take from out of the middle of the Jordan, out of the place where the priests’ feet stood firm, twelve stones, carry them over with you, and lay them down in the place where you’ll camp tonight.’ ”
Joshua set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests who bore the ark of the covenant stood; and they are there to this day.
The garrison of the Philistines went out to the pass of Michmash.

Now it fell on a day, that Jonathan the son of Saul said to the young man who bore his armor, “Come! Let’s go over to the Philistines’ garrison that is on the other side.” But he didn’t tell his father.

Between the passes, by which Jonathan sought to go over to the Philistines’ garrison, there was a rocky crag on the one side, and a rocky crag on the other side: and the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.

Jonathan said to the young man who bore his armor, “Come! Let’s go over to the garrison of these uncircumcised. It may be that Yahweh will work for us; for there is no restraint on Yahweh to save by many or by few.”
Both of them revealed themselves to the garrison of the Philistines: and the Philistines said, “Behold, the Hebrews are coming out of the holes where they had hidden themselves!”
There was a trembling in the camp, in the field, and among all the people; the garrison, and the raiders, also trembled; and the earth quaked, so there was an exceedingly great trembling.
David was then in the stronghold; and the garrison of the Philistines was then in Bethlehem.
I will thrust you from your office. You will be pulled down from your station.
